angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 996,242 km at 161.55 pc = 0.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.1902 +/- 0.0176 mas (same row, RUWE 0.89): 161.55 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.432 +/- 0.092 solar radii from Southworth et al. 2011, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of WASP-7 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2011A&A...527A...8S/abstract): 996,242 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.276 +/- 0.065 solar masses from Southworth et al. 2011, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-7 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2011A&A...527A...8S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6400 +/- 100 K from Southworth et al. 2011, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-7 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2011A&A...527A...8S/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Southworth et al. 2011, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-7 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2011A&A...527A...8S/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-7.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.232, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
